examples.ko: 시베리아는 겨울에 꽁꽁 언 동토로 변해요.
examples.en: In winter, Siberia turns into frozen land.
The frozen ground is melting because of climate change.
An expedition team went to the Arctic to study the frozen ground.

examples.ko: 그곳은 일 년 내내 얼어붙은 동토예요.
examples.en: That place is frozen land all year round.

examples.ko: 동토 아래에는 오래된 식물이 묻혀 있어요.
examples.en: Ancient plants are buried beneath the frozen ground.
There are plants that bloom even in frozen land.

explain: 북극이나 시베리아처럼 땅이 얼어 있는 곳을 말할 때 뉴스나 과학 글에서 써요. 일상에서는 '얼어붙은 땅'이라고 해요. '영구 동토'라는 표현으로도 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 영구 동토가 녹으면 온실가스가 나올 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If the permafrost melts, greenhouse gases can be released.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동토'가 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most frequent pairing with 동토.

phrases.example: 동토 지대에는 나무가 잘 자라지 않아요.
phrases.en: Trees don't grow well in frozen-ground regions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅이 언 지역을 가리킬 때 '지대'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '지대' to refer to a region where the ground is frozen.

phrases.example: 얼어붙은 땅에서는 농사를 지을 수 없어요.
phrases.en: You can't farm on frozen ground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '동토' 대신 이렇게 쉽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, people say this simpler phrase instead of 동토.

explain_en: Frozen ground in very cold regions, such as permafrost (시베리아의 동토) It is used in news and science writing for places where the ground is frozen, such as the Arctic or Siberia. In daily speech people say '얼어붙은 땅'. It also often appears in the expression '영구 동토' (permafrost).

examples.ko: 만조 때는 바닷물이 이 길까지 올라와요.
examples.en: At high tide, the seawater comes up to this road.
It's dangerous to go onto the mudflat at high tide.
Today's high tide is around three in the afternoon.
When it's high tide, the boats come into the harbor.
It's an area with a big difference between high and low tide.
We decided to set sail to match the high tide.

explain: 바닷물이 가장 높이 올라온 때예요. 반대말은 '간조'이고, '만조와 간조'로 같이 말하는 일이 많아요. 갯벌 체험이나 낚시 정보에서 시간을 알려 줄 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Check the high-tide time before going to the mudflats.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간 정보를 말할 때 자주 붙는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when giving time information.

phrases.example: 만조와 간조는 하루에 두 번씩 있어요.
phrases.en: High tide and low tide happen twice a day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말과 함께 묶어서 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said together with its opposite.

phrases.en: When it is high tide, the road floods.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷물이 가장 높아지는 때가 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the time comes when the seawater is at its highest.

explain_en: It is the time when the sea level is at its highest. The opposite is '간조', and the two are often said together as '만조와 간조'. It often appears when giving times for mudflat trips or fishing.

examples.ko: 산불이 난 뒤에 그 산은 민둥산이 되었어요.
examples.en: After the wildfire, that mountain became bare.

examples.ko: 나무를 베어 낸 산이 민둥산으로 변했어요.
examples.en: The mountain where trees were cut turned into a barren hill.

examples.ko: 나무가 없는 민둥산에서는 비가 오면 흙이 쓸려 내려가요.
examples.en: On a bare mountain without trees, soil washes away when it rains.
From far away, the top looked empty like a bare mountain.

examples.ko: 사람들이 나무를 심어서 민둥산을 다시 숲으로 만들었어요.
examples.en: People planted trees and turned the bare mountain back into forest.
A bare mountain has no shade, so it's hard to hike.

explain: 나무나 풀이 거의 없는 산을 말하고, 비슷한 말로 '벌거숭이산'도 있어요. 산불이나 벌목 뒤에 변한 모습을 이야기할 때 자주 써요. 반대로 나무가 많은 산은 '숲이 우거진 산'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 비가 오면 벌거숭이산은 흙이 무너질 수 있어요.
phrases.en: When it rains, soil on a bare mountain can collapse.
phrases.nuance_ko: '민둥산'과 같은 뜻의 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A synonym with the same meaning as 민둥산.

phrases.en: An event was held to plant trees on a bare mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무 없는 산을 다시 푸르게 만드는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the work of making a treeless mountain green again.
phrases.en_equiv: to plant trees on a bare hill

phrases.en: A mountain with thick forest is cool in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 민둥산과 반대로 나무가 많은 산을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of a bare mountain: one full of trees.

explain_en: It refers to a mountain with almost no trees or grass, and '벌거숭이산' is a similar word. It is often used for how a mountain looks after a wildfire or logging. A mountain full of trees is described as '숲이 우거진 산'.

examples.ko: 장마철에는 댐 방류 때문에 강가가 위험해요.
examples.en: During the rainy season, the riverside is dangerous because of dam releases.

examples.ko: 방류 소식에 주민들이 높은 곳으로 대피했어요.
examples.en: On hearing news of the release, residents evacuated to higher ground.

examples.ko: 어린 물고기 방류 행사가 강에서 열렸어요.
examples.en: An event releasing young fish was held at the river.

examples.ko: 공장 폐수 방류 문제로 주민들이 항의했어요.
examples.en: Residents protested over the problem of factory wastewater discharge.

examples.ko: 방류가 시작되기 전에 안내 방송이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A public announcement was made before the release began.
I saw news that they reduced the amount of water released.

explain: 댐의 물, 물고기, 폐수 같은 것을 밖으로 흘려보내는 일이에요. 뉴스에서 '댐 방류', '치어 방류'처럼 많이 들어요. 동사는 '방류하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 와서 댐 방류량을 늘렸어요.
phrases.en: Because of heavy rain, they increased the dam's discharge volume.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흘려보내는 물의 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the amount of water being released.

phrases.example: 봄마다 강에서 치어 방류 행사가 열려요.
phrases.en: Every spring, a young-fish release event is held at the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새끼 물고기를 강이나 바다에 놓아주는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Releasing young fish into a river or the sea.

phrases.en: An announcement about the dam discharge was broadcast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 내보내기 전에 사람들에게 알리는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A notice given to people before water is released.

explain_en: It means letting things such as dam water, fish or wastewater flow out. You hear it often in the news in phrases like '댐 방류' and '치어 방류'. The verb is '방류하다'.

t90.ax: An event releasing young fish was held at the river.

en: to be emitted; to be discharged; to be produced

examples.en: A lot of smoke is released from the factory.
The gas emitted from cars is a problem.
They say harmful substances are flushed out through sweat.
All the water drained out through the sewer.

examples.ko: 더러운 공기가 밖으로 배출될 수 있게 창문을 열어요.
examples.en: I open the window so the stale air can get out.
They say your body feels lighter once toxins are flushed out.

explain: '배출되다'는 안에 있던 가스·물·노폐물이 밖으로 나갈 때 써요. 환경 뉴스에서 '이산화탄소가 배출되다'처럼 자주 나와요. 하는 쪽을 말할 때는 '배출하다'를 쓰고, 쓰레기를 내놓는 일도 '쓰레기를 배출하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이 학교에서는 훌륭한 인재가 많이 배출돼요.
phrases.en: Many talented people come out of this school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물질이 아니라 사람이 한 곳에서 계속 나올 때도 써요. 학교나 지역이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for people, not just substances, who keep coming out of one place. The subject is a school or region.

explain_en: Passive, waste or fumes expelled; also talent produced (인재가 배출되다) 배출되다 is used when gas, water, or waste leaves from inside. In environmental news you often see 이산화탄소가 배출되다. When you name the one doing it, use 배출하다, which also covers putting out trash, as in 쓰레기를 배출하다.

t90.ax: The gas emitted from cars is a problem.

examples.en: The factory emits smoke.
You must put out trash on the designated days.
The body releases heat through sweat.

examples.ko: 이 대학은 훌륭한 인재를 많이 배출했어요.
examples.en: This university has produced many fine talents.

examples.ko: 차가 배출하는 가스를 줄이는 방법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned how to reduce the gas that cars emit.
Please put out food waste separately.

explain: 안에 있는 것을 밖으로 내보내는 말이에요. 쓰레기는 '버리다'가 일상적이고, 분리수거에서는 '배출하다'가 공식 표현이에요. 공장의 연기와 가스, 몸의 땀과 노폐물에도 써요. 학교나 팀에서 인재나 선수가 계속 나오는 것도 '배출하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Please put out the trash after 7 p.m.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분리수거나 아파트 안내문에서 쓰는 공식 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official expression in recycling rules and apartment notices.

phrases.en: Cars emit harmful gases.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공장이나 차가 연기나 가스를 밖으로 내보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when factories or cars let smoke or gas out.

phrases.example: 이 학교는 훌륭한 선수를 많이 배출했어요.
phrases.en: This school has produced many great athletes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 팀에서 뛰어난 사람이 계속 나온다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a school or team keeps producing outstanding people.

explain_en: Active, someone or something expels waste, gas, pollutants (가스를 배출하다) It means sending something inside out. For trash, '버리다' is everyday while '배출하다' is the official term in recycling rules. It also fits factory smoke and gas, and sweat and waste leaving the body. It is also used for a school or team 'producing' talented people one after another.

examples.ko: 올해는 비가 많이 와서 병충해가 걱정이에요.
examples.en: It rained a lot this year, so I'm worried about crop disease and pests.
The farmers sprayed pesticide to stop disease and pests.

examples.ko: 이 품종은 병충해에 강해서 키우기 쉬워요.
examples.en: This variety resists disease and pests, so it's easy to grow.

examples.ko: 병충해 피해 때문에 사과 값이 많이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Apple prices rose a lot because of damage from disease and pests.

examples.ko: 병충해로 배추 농사를 망친 분이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people lost their cabbage harvest to disease and pests.
What do I do if disease or pests show up in my garden plot?

explain: 병(식물의 병)과 충해(벌레 피해)를 합친 말이라 농작물, 나무, 과일 이야기에서 주로 나와요. '병해충'이라고 순서를 바꿔 말하기도 해요. '병충해 피해', '병충해 방제'처럼 뉴스에서 자주 짝을 이뤄요.

phrases.en: The apple trees suffered pest and disease damage this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농작물이 병이나 벌레 피해를 받았다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means crops suffered damage from disease or pests.

phrases.en: In spring, we carry out pest and disease control work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병과 벌레를 막고 없애는 일을 말하고 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means preventing and removing disease and pests; common in the news.

phrases.en: Farmers are worried because diseases and pests are increasing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '병충해'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만, 피해보다 병과 해충 자체를 가리킬 때 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used much like 병충해, but more often refers to the diseases and pests themselves than to the damage.

explain_en: It combines plant disease and insect damage, so it appears mostly when talking about crops, trees and fruit. People also say '병해충' with the order swapped. It pairs with words like '병충해 피해' and '병충해 방제' in the news.

examples.en: A lot of dust blows around at the construction site.
I have to wear a mask because of the dust.
They installed a device to reduce dust in the workplace.

examples.ko: 분진에 오래 노출되면 폐에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Long exposure to dust is bad for the lungs.
I vacuumed up the dust in the room.

examples.ko: 분진은 눈에 잘 안 보여도 건강에 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: Even if dust is hard to see, it affects your health.

explain: 집에서는 보통 '먼지'라고 하고, '분진'은 공사장, 공장, 광산처럼 작업 환경에서 날리는 가루 먼지를 말할 때 많이 써요. 뉴스나 안전 안내문에 자주 나와요. '미세먼지'와 같은 말은 아니에요.

phrases.en: There is a lot of dust in the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이나 일상에서는 '분진'보다 '먼지'를 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: At home and in daily life, 먼지 is used far more than 분진.

phrases.en: We wear dust masks at the work site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작업 환경에서 쓰는 마스크를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for masks worn in work environments.

phrases.en: Dust was produced at the factory, so we closed the windows.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 뉴스에서 쓰는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression used in notices and news.

explain_en: Technical — fine particles from construction or industry. At home people just say '먼지', while '분진' is used more for powdery dust in work settings such as construction sites, factories and mines. It often appears in news and safety notices. It is not the same word as '미세먼지' (fine dust).

t90.ax: I vacuumed up the dust in the room.

en: to be collapsed; to be broken down; to crumble

examples.en: The old bridge suddenly collapsed.
The building almost collapsed in the earthquake.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 산이 붕괴되는 일이 있어요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, hillsides sometimes collapse.

examples.ko: 가족이 아프자 우리 집 생활이 붕괴돼 버렸어요.
examples.en: When a family member got sick, our household life fell apart.
They rescued people from inside the collapsed building.
Once trust crumbles, it is hard to rebuild.

explain: '무너지다'가 일상에서 쓰는 말이고, '붕괴되다'는 뉴스나 글에서 건물, 다리, 제도, 관계가 크게 무너질 때 써요. 이미 '되다'가 붙은 말이라 '붕괴되어지다'처럼 겹쳐 쓰지 않아요. 누가 일부러 무너뜨릴 때는 '무너뜨리다'를 써요.

phrases.en: This building is at risk of collapsing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전 문제를 경고하는 뉴스나 안내문에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in news or notices warning about safety.

phrases.en: I was shocked to see the news of the collapse accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '붕괴'가 앞에 붙어 사고 이름을 만들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun 붕괴 comes first to form the name of an accident.

phrases.en: The old wall collapsed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 자연스럽게 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word that sounds more natural in everyday speech.

explain_en: Passive: a structure or system falls down (bridge, building) 무너지다 is the everyday word. 붕괴되다 is for news and writing, when buildings, bridges, systems, or relationships collapse on a large scale. It already has the passive 되다, so don't double it as 붕괴되어지다. When someone brings something down on purpose, use 무너뜨리다.

examples.en: The bridge suddenly collapsed.
There is a risk that the old building will collapse.
When it rains a lot, the mountain road gives way.

examples.ko: 시장이 붕괴하는 바람에 많은 회사가 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: Because the market collapsed, many companies closed.

examples.ko: 붕괴한 곳에서 구조 작업이 계속되고 있어요.
examples.en: Rescue work continues at the site of the collapse.

examples.ko: 믿음이 붕괴하고 나서 둘은 다시 만나지 않았어요.
examples.en: After their trust collapsed, the two never met again.

explain: '무너지다'는 건물·마음·벽 어디에나 쓰는 일상어이고, 붕괴하다는 뉴스에서 건물·제도·경제처럼 큰 것이 무너질 때 써요. 명사 '붕괴'는 '붕괴 사고'처럼 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: The building collapsed because of the heavy rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '붕괴하다'와 뜻이 거의 같고, 뉴스에서는 '붕괴되다'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as 붕괴하다; 붕괴되다 is more common in the news.

phrases.en: The road was blocked because of the collapse accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing common in the news.

phrases.en: The old wall fell down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 일상에서 더 자유롭게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but used more freely in daily life.

explain_en: Active form: buildings, systems or order collapse. '무너지다' (fall down) is the everyday word for buildings, hearts, or walls; 붕괴하다 is used in the news for big things collapsing, such as a building, a system, or an economy. The noun 붕괴 often appears as in '붕괴 사고' (collapse accident).

examples.ko: 바다의 산성화가 산호에게 큰 피해를 줘요.
examples.en: Ocean acidification does great harm to corals.
People spread lime to prevent soil acidification.

examples.ko: 산성화로 호수 속 물고기가 줄어들고 있어요.
examples.en: Fish in the lake are decreasing because of acidification.
Acidification is also related to air pollution.

examples.ko: 해양 산성화에 대한 뉴스를 읽고 걱정했어요.
examples.en: I read news about ocean acidification and felt worried.

examples.ko: 산성화 속도가 빨라져서 연구자들이 조사에 나섰어요.
examples.en: The pace of acidification has sped up, so researchers started investigating.

explain: 주로 환경 뉴스에서 바다, 토양, 호수가 점점 산성이 되는 것을 말할 때 나와요. '해양 산성화', '토양 산성화'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여 써요. 학교 과학 시간이나 기후 변화 이야기에서도 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 해양 산성화 때문에 산호가 줄고 있어요.
phrases.en: Corals are declining because of ocean acidification.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다가 산성으로 변하는 현상을 가리키는 정해진 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set term for the phenomenon of oceans becoming acidic.

phrases.en: The lake's acidification got worse, so the fish decreased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산성이 되는 정도가 더 커질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the degree of acidification increases.

phrases.en: They spread lime to prevent the soil from acidifying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경이 산성으로 변하지 않게 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means keeping the environment from turning acidic.

explain_en: It mainly appears in environmental news about seas, soil and lakes gradually becoming acidic. The affected thing is placed in front, as in '해양 산성화' and '토양 산성화'. You may also hear it in school science class or in talk about climate change.

examples.en: If seawater acidifies, shells become weaker.

examples.ko: 토양이 산성화해서 농작물이 잘 자라지 못해요.
examples.en: The soil has acidified, so crops don't grow well.
They are investigating why the lake is acidifying.

examples.ko: 이산화탄소가 늘면 바다가 더 빨리 산성화해요.
examples.en: When carbon dioxide increases, the ocean acidifies faster.

examples.ko: 산성화한 땅에는 석회를 뿌려 주면 좋아요.
examples.en: It helps to spread lime on acidified land.
I tested whether the pond had become acidic.

explain: '바다가/땅이/호수가 산성화하다'처럼 환경이 산성으로 변할 때 써요. 환경 뉴스나 과학 수업에서 주로 들어요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.

phrases.en: The lake became acidified, so the fish decreased.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산성화하다'의 피동 표현으로 환경이 변한 결과를 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form of 산성화하다, more natural when describing the result of an environmental change.

phrases.en: The ocean is gradually acidifying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금도 변하는 중이라는 진행의 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows an ongoing change that is still happening.

phrases.en: We always manage the water so it does not acidify.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산성으로 변하지 않는 상태를 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form describing the state of not turning acidic.

explain_en: It is used when an environment turns acidic, as in '바다가/땅이/호수가 산성화하다'. You mostly hear it in environmental news or science class. It is rarely used in daily conversation.

examples.en: The team completed its mission even in terrible weather.
All flights were canceled because of bad weather.
The bad weather continued, so we canceled the hike.
The ship ran into bad weather and returned to port.
The game was held as scheduled despite the bad weather.
This equipment works well even in bad weather.

explain: 폭우, 폭설, 강풍처럼 활동에 지장을 주는 심한 날씨를 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '날씨가 안 좋다'고 하고, '악천후'는 뉴스, 일기예보, 안내문에서 자주 나와요. '악천후 속에서', '악천후로 인해'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The game continued even in bad weather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 날씨 한가운데에서 일어난 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something happening in the middle of bad weather.

phrases.en: The ship could not leave because of bad weather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 안내문에서 이유를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news and notices to state a reason.

phrases.en: The event will be held as planned even in bad weather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 날씨와 상관없이 이루어진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something happens regardless of the bad weather.

explain_en: It means severe weather such as heavy rain, snow or strong wind that interferes with activities. In everyday talk people say '날씨가 안 좋다', while '악천후' appears in news, forecasts and notices. It is used as '악천후 속에서' or '악천후로 인해'.

examples.en: Ammonia has a very strong smell.

examples.ko: 화장실을 청소할 때 암모니아 냄새가 나서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: I opened the window because of the ammonia smell while cleaning the bathroom.
We did an ammonia experiment in science class.

examples.ko: 이 세제에는 암모니아가 들어 있어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: This cleaner contains ammonia, so you have to be careful.
In farming, fertilizer is made from ammonia.

examples.ko: 암모니아를 마시면 위험하니까 아이 손이 닿지 않게 하세요.
examples.en: Ammonia is dangerous to swallow, so keep it out of children's reach.

explain: 외래어라 영어 ammonia와 거의 같은 소리예요. 주로 과학 시간이나 청소용품 설명에서 보고, 코를 찌르는 냄새와 같이 말해요. 다른 세제와 섞으면 위험하다는 안내도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The room smells like ammonia.
phrases.nuance_ko: 코를 찌르는 냄새를 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for a sharp, pungent smell.

phrases.en: This cleaner contains ammonia.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품 성분을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when explaining a product's ingredients.

phrases.en: It is dangerous to breathe ammonia gas.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학이나 안전 안내에서 자주 보는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in science lessons and safety warnings.

explain_en: It is a loanword, nearly the same sound as English ammonia. You mostly meet it in science class or on cleaning-product labels, usually with its sharp smell. Warnings about not mixing it with other cleaners are also common.

examples.en: This sea is famous as a squid fishing ground.
The fishing ground is far, so the boat takes several days.
After the typhoon passed, the fish in the fishing ground decreased.

examples.ko: 새로운 어장을 찾으려고 어부들이 먼 바다로 나갔어요.
examples.en: The fishermen went out to the far sea to find a new fishing ground.

examples.ko: 어장 근처에서는 낚시를 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not fish near the fishing ground.
Many boats go back and forth between fishing grounds.

explain: 물고기를 잡는 바다나 강의 구역을 말하고, '어촌', '어부'와 같이 바다 일을 말할 때 나와요. 양식하는 곳은 '양식장'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 비유 표현도 있어서 아래에서 같이 알아 두세요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 어장 관리를 한다고 친구들이 말해요.
phrases.en: My friends say that person keeps several people on the hook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 없으면서 여러 사람이 자기를 좋아하게 두고 관심을 주는 행동을 말하는 입말이에요. 보통 비판하는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spoken phrase for keeping several people interested without really having feelings for them. It is usually critical.

explain_en: It refers to the sea or river area where fish are caught, and appears with words like '어촌' (fishing village) and '어부' (fisherman). A place where fish are farmed is called '양식장', which is different. It also has a figurative use, so see below.
